correctness.rationale: Ziegler theorem 2.3 (1994 preprint pp1,8) gives simply-connected pure two-complexes for n>=5. A face has at most one vertex of each row so all simplex stabilizers act pointwise; the fixed loci are exactly empty, three vertices or Δ(3,2)≅S¹. Armstrong gives π1=1 for all odd dihedral subgroups and π1=C2 for even full dihedral action. Burnside/orbit cell counts yield χ. A 2-dimensional simply connected CW complex is a wedge of 2-spheres; H2 of any 2-complex is free. The integral Bockstein for H1=C2 reduces to nonzero u² and gives category two. Standalone orbit-chain enumeration with integer Smith form checks n=5..12; finite checks are corroboration only.

Ziegler provides cover shellability, Armstrong supplies only the general group-theoretic tool, and the published cyclic 4x5 and 5x5 quotients concern different spaces. No identified published-finding corpus result covers the all-odd-dihedral-subgroup formula or the odd/even normalized category transition. Residual prior-art uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete homotopy classification for all odd reflection-containing dihedral subgroups of a classical stable-range chessboard family, plus an even/odd fundamental-group and mod-two cup-product transition with exact normalized LS category for all widths >=5. The geometric reflection classification produces a parity obstruction invisible to cover homology; specific sphere multiplicities and category were not implied by the smaller n=4 quotient table. The claim does not rely on arbitrary finite cutoffs or raw enumeration.
